_: Truss, risers and screens, shared by both previz renderers. previz/src/scene.rs reads this with include_str! + serde; ui/src/components/Previz3D.tsx imports it directly. Same reason as shared/figure.json: the two views had drifted, and here it was the WEB that was richer — it drew a truss lattice, a two-tone riser and a framed screen while the native view drew all four kinds as one plain box. Lengths metres, angles radians.
_materials: Truss metallic is 0.30, not the 0.75 the web used. A metal's colour is what it reflects and neither scene has an environment map, so 0.75 renders as a black bar in the native window.
_truss: A lattice RULE rather than a table, because a placed truss carries its own section from the patch while an inferred run is a fixed 0.29 m. Ratios are relative to the section: chord radius = section * chordRatio (0.025 at 0.29, the value the inferred runs were authored with, so that path renders identically), web member radius = chord * webRatio, and one bay per section * bayRatio (0.5 m at 0.29). Four chords at the section corners; zigzag webbing on the two vertical faces and the underside — a real truss webs all four, but nobody is ever above the top one — plus a vertical rung at each node, which is what stops the zigzag reading as a lightning bolt.
_riser: A skirt the full height with a deck slab forming its TOP. The slab's top face must stay exactly at y + size.h and must not overhang the skirt: buildOccluders, standingHeightAt and floor_height_at all treat a riser as one box from y to y + h with no notion of sub-parts, so a slab sitting proud silently desyncs beam cutting from where a performer's feet are put. Centring the slab ON y + h is exactly the 25 mm bug fixed in bd67d28.
_screen: A dark face inside a frame, both staying INSIDE the declared box so the beam occluder and the plan hit-test — which both take w x h x d as truth — are not lying. bezel is how far the face is inset in w and h; faceDepth is the fraction of depth the face occupies; faceProud is how far its front stands ahead of the frame's. That last one is not styling: give them the same front plane and they z-fight into a dithered mess.
_trussLegFoot: A base plate under a standing leg, spread x its section.
